# A sum of two-limb numbers with a bound of its error

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `add_ball_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x + y$ with a bound $d$ of its error:

$$\lvert (x + y) - z\rvert \le d.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`add_down_2_2`](add_down_2_2.md), [`add_up_2_2`](add_up_2_2.md), [`ball_contains_ball_2`](ball_contains_ball_2.md), [`ball_contains_point_2`](ball_contains_point_2.md), [`ball_equal_2`](ball_equal_2.md), [`interval_mid_rad_2`](interval_mid_rad_2.md), [`ball_less_2`](ball_less_2.md), [`ball_less_equal_2`](ball_less_equal_2.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x + y\rvert$.
- $\lvert (x + y) - z\rvert \le d$: $d$ bounds the error of $z$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\frac{3}{2^{106} - 2^{55}} \approx 3.6978 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\frac{3}{2^{48} - 2^{26}} \approx 1.0658 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.8000000000004p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.800008p-47f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.8000000000004p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.800008p-47f`, `0.0f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_ball_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Directed2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Directed2.v), against `add_ball_2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions add_ball_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_ball_2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(z0, z1, d) := add_ball_2_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  fmt emin prec d /\
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1))) <= (3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1)) /\
  Rabs (((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1)) - (z0 + z1)) <= d.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `add_ball_2_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_2_2 with the radius of ball_add_2 for radii zero (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_ball_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_ball_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md).

```
# The sum of two 2-limb numbers with a bound d of its own error, |(x + y) - z| <= d
# (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Bounds of two limbs"). d is the radius that ball_add_2
# returns for radii zero, with the same three constants E, G, H: there s = add(0, 0) = 0 and
# t = fma(az, E, 0), which is prod(az, E). So the statement is ball_add_2_correct after two
# rewritings, with the error bound of add_2_2 for z. The operands are points: the encloses claim
# names no ball.

(z0, z1) = add_2_2(x0, x1, y0, y1)
az       = abs(z0)
t        = prod(az, const up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u)))
d        = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_contains_ball_2`](ball_contains_ball_2.md) and [`ball_contains_point_2`](ball_contains_point_2.md) and [`ball_equal_2`](ball_equal_2.md) and [`interval_mid_rad_2`](interval_mid_rad_2.md) and [`ball_less_2`](ball_less_2.md) and [`ball_less_equal_2`](ball_less_equal_2.md) states that, and the public headers do not call them yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
